title: Why you overthink at 3 a.m.
description:
Why does a small worry feel enormous in the middle of the night? Researchers have proposed the "mind after midnight" hypothesis: in the early hours, thinking tends to lean negative and judgment gets weaker. It is a hypothesis, not a settled fact.

Source: Tubbs, Perlis & Basner, "Mind After Midnight: Nocturnal Wakefulness, Behavioral Dysregulation, and Psychopathology", Frontiers in Network Physiology.

#shorts #psychology #sleep

scenes.headline: 3 A.M.
scenes.text: Why does a small worry feel enormous at three in the morning?

scenes.headline: MIND AFTER MIDNIGHT
scenes.text: Researchers have proposed an idea called the mind after midnight hypothesis.

scenes.headline: NIGHT VS MORNING
scenes.text: In the early hours, thinking seems to lean negative and judgment gets weaker, while you're tired and alone with your thoughts.

scenes.headline: JUST A HYPOTHESIS
scenes.text: It's a hypothesis, not a settled fact.

scenes.headline: SLEEP ON IT
scenes.text: So if a problem feels huge at night, give it a night's sleep before you decide how big it really is.
